newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Libya offers Kuwait Airways pilots to beat strike.
newsitem.headline: Libya offers Kuwait Airways pilots to beat strike.

text.p: Libya, which is under a U.N. air embargo, has offered Libyan pilots to Kuwait Airways Corp (KAC) to beat a strike by Kuwaiti pilots and engineers, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Al-Rai al-Aam newspaper reported that the offer was made by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi. The United Nations placed an air and arms embargo against Libya in 1992 over the alleged involvement of two Libyan agents in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Scotland.
KAC has said that the one-day strike which started at 0700 a.m. (0400 GMT) on Tuesday had cost it $1.3 million and affected 18 outbound flights from the Gulf Arab state.
The Kuwait Aircraft Engineers and Pilots Association plans a complete stoppage every Tuesday and delays to all outbound flights by one hour during the week.
"The industrial action will affect Kuwait Airways only," the association said in a statement issued on Tuesday.
It said the strike was due to the "failure of negotiations and prolonged deliberations by government committees which have lasted for more than a year without reaching an acceptable settlement".
It is demanding "adjustment of salaries, allowances and restoration of certain benefits".
The association in November agreed to postpone flight-delay action after talks with the country's crown prince and prime minister, Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah.

Kuwait Airways said on Tuesday that the wages of Kuwaiti pilots and engineers were already "distingushed". It said a pilot earns 3,400 dinars ($11,300) a month, a co-pilot is paid 2,570 dinars, and engineers make 1,600 dinars a month.
In March KAC said it total income was 98.5 million dinars in the six months to December 1996 compared with expenditures of 111 million dinars.
Some 9.1 million dinars of the deficit were spent on debt servicing. KAC made a loss of 35 million dinars in the fiscal year ending June 1996 compared with 27.9 million dinars the previous year.
KAC has a fleet of 15 Airbus Industries aircraft all bought after the 1991 Gulf War and two Boeing Co 747s which will be replaced by two Boeing 777s on order.
